source_request: Photograph an adult road worker rolling the existing asphalt road surface into a low curl with both palms. Keep the lane marking bending with the road and the curled strip unbroken from the pavement behind it.
interpreted_intent: An ordinary street surface becomes physically rollable while retaining its road identity
subject: One adult road worker manipulating the actual asphalt road surface
setting: A street with a painted lane marking and intact surrounding pavement
event: The worker rolls a continuous strip of the existing road surface into a low curl with both palms
visual_priorities: Both palms visibly bear against the same asphalt curl
The asphalt strip and lane marking remain continuous with the road
The underside, compressed grit, and cast shadow communicate thickness and bending
A supported kneeling posture and clear three-quarter view preserve body readability
baseline_prompt_en: A street-level photograph shows an adult road worker slowly rolling the actual asphalt surface into a low curl beside a painted lane marking. The worker kneels on both knees, shins resting on intact pavement, with their torso upright and centered above their knees. Both bare hands rest on the same broad curl, palms forward, fingers spread over its upper face, wrists straight and elbows softly bent. The asphalt remains one unbroken strip connected to the road behind the curl; the painted line bends with it. Compressed grit, a dark underside, and the curl's cast shadow make its thickness readable. An unobstructed three-quarter view shows both hands, both arms, both knees, and the continuous connection.
